target.title: fix(scripts): bound gh CLI helper subprocess calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`scripts/lib/plain-gh.mjs` is the central helper for invoking the `gh` CLI across many repo scripts. All three functions (`execPlainGh`, `execGhApiRead`, `spawnPlainGh`) call `execFileSync`/`spawnSync` without a timeout. Every `gh` CLI invocation reaches the GitHub API over the network — a stalled TCP connection, unresponsive API endpoint, or proxy timeout can hang the calling script indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a 30-second default timeout (`PLAIN_GH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`) to all three helper functions. Callers can override via `options.timeout` when a longer deadline is needed.

This follows the same pattern as other network-operation bound PRs:
- `fix(ci): bound release evidence dispatch` (#108898)
- `fix(ci): bound plugin npm artifact connection` (#108897)

## User Impact

All scripts that use `plain-gh.mjs` (PR creation, release evidence, CI checks, etc.) are now protected from network hangs.

## Evidence

- 3 functions updated, all following the same `options.timeout ?? DEFAULT` pattern
- Callers can override when needed
- No test changes needed (these are script helpers)

target.title: feat(skills): preview proposals before approval
target.body:
Closes #103871

## Summary

- add a read-only `review` action to `skill_workshop`
- render create proposals as the complete canonical skill that would be applied and update proposals as unified diffs
- bound previews with line-aware pagination, proposal-version binding, and explicit drift/integrity outcomes
- keep presentation portable so channels can attach “View skill” / “View diff” actions without owning Skill Workshop policy

## Problem

Approval messages currently provide only a prose summary. Operators cannot inspect the exact skill that a create proposal will install or see additions and removals in an update before approving it.

## Design and safety

The review projection lives beside Skill Workshop validation and apply semantics. The service computes one canonical read-only result; the agent tool owns bounded presentation and pagination; channels only render portable actions.

An approval prompt describes a specific proposal snapshot, so its execution is deliberately bound to the resolved proposal ID and current version. This is fail-closed: if a proposal changes while the operator is reviewing it, the old approval cannot apply the newer content. A code-site invariant now documents this coupling. Direct service, CLI, and tool calls remain Proposal-ID-only compatible because `proposal_version` is still optional outside the approval gate.

## User impact

- create proposals can be reviewed in full before approval
- update proposals show an exact unified diff
- Approve and Reject remain available on every preview page, including page 1
- stale approval prompts fail with expected/current version feedback

target.title: fix(nostr): strip internal tool-trace banners from outbound text
target.body:
Part of #90684

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Nostr users receiving bot replies would see internal assistant tool-trace scaffolding lines (e.g. `⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed`) leaked into outbound messages. These banners are internal runtime diagnostics that should not reach end users.

Nostr has two user-visible reply paths: the shared outbound adapter and the gateway inbound DM `deliver` callback. Both could forward raw assistant text before this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` on:
1. `nostrOutboundAdapter.sanitizeText` (shared outbound delivery path)
2. the inbound DM `deliver` callback before markdown table conversion (the main bot-reply path for incoming Nostr DMs)

Also drop inbound replies that become empty after sanitization so blank encrypted DMs are not published.

Matches the accepted sibling pattern already shipped for Slack, Signal, Matrix, Feishu, Mattermost, Telegram, Google Chat, QQBot, IRC, SMS, Discord, WhatsApp, LINE, and Nextcloud Talk.

Non-goals: no relay protocol redesign; no committed proof harness in this PR.

Collision check: searched open/closed PRs for nostr tool-trace / `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` / #90684 — this is the Nostr channel candidate under the cross-channel sanitizer issue. Siblings: merged [#101708](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101708) (LINE), [#101712](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101712) (Nextcloud Talk), [#98705](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98705) (Feishu).

## User Impact

- **Before:** Tool-trace failure banners could appear in Nostr bot replies on outbound delivery and inbound DM replies; trace-only replies could publish empty encrypted DMs.
- **After:** Banners are stripped on both paths; fully stripped inbound replies are dropped. Normal assistant prose and markdown table conversion are preserved.

## Evidence

Exact head: `0193ff493de8d5f99452aa5eb95ab2d5e74e0960`

### current-`main` negative (core strip keeps banner)

Core `stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding` does not remove tool-trace failure banners (same pre-fix leak class as sibling channel PRs).

### Non-mocked loopback relay delivery (local harness — not shipped)

Local WebSocket Nostr relay + real `startNostrBus.sendDm` encrypt/publish, applying production `nostrOutboundAdapter.sanitizeText` / inbound `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText`, then decrypting captured kind-4 EVENTs. No third-party relay and no personal nsec. Harness kept local (not committed).

```text

head=555b997a4793c43a71c527b2bb27e5f9c4ba5596 (proof captured pre-drop of local harness; behavior unchanged)

PASS outbound_adapter_wire_clean plain="Done."
PASS outbound_trace_only_no_event
PASS inbound_deliver_wire_clean plain="Done."
PASS inbound_trace_only_dropped
{
  "scenario": "nostr loopback relay tool-trace sanitize",
  "relay": "ws://127.0.0.1:34059",
  "assertions": 5,
  "capturedEvents": 3,
  "paths": [
    "outbound.sanitizeText+sendDm",
    "inbound.sanitizeAssistantVisibleText+reply"
  ]
}
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 5 passed, 0 failed
```

### Focused tests

```bash

```

```text

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard
```

## Verification

- Exact head: `0193ff493de8d5f99452aa5eb95ab2d5e74e0960`
- Rebased onto recent `origin/main`
- Focused tests: 6 passed
- Loopback relay proof: 5/5 assertions (local harness, not in diff)
- No proof script in PR diff (avoids extension boundary / lint gates)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** tool-trace banners stripped before Nostr DM encrypt/publish on outbound + inbound deliver; trace-only dropped.
- **Environment:** local Linux WSL2; loopback `ws://127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>` relay; real `nostr-tools` encrypt/publish/decrypt.
- **Observed output after fix:** (proof paste above)
- **What was not tested:** credentialed round-trip against a public third-party relay / personal nsec.

## Risk / Compatibility

**Low/Med (message-delivery).** Only changes assistant-visible text shaping on Nostr outbound/inbound deliver. Mitigation: sibling-channel pattern + loopback decrypt proof + focused gateway/outbound tests.

- Manually reviewed and verified

target.title: fix(ui): avoid splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs in session display peer-id tail
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the sidebar display name for an unnamed direct-message session could emit isolated UTF-16 surrogate halves when the peer id contains astral characters (e.g., emoji).

## Why This Change Was Made

`shortenPeerId` sliced the tail of the identifier with raw `String.prototype.slice(-6)`, which can bisect surrogate pairs. It now uses the repository's existing `sliceUtf16Safe` helper so the shortened tail always falls on a valid UTF-16 boundary.

## User Impact

Session labels in the Control UI sidebar remain well-formed when peer identifiers contain non-BMP characters.

## Evidence

- Replaced `trimmed.slice(-6)` with `sliceUtf16Safe(trimmed, -6)` in `ui/src/lib/session-display.ts`.
- Added a regression test in `ui/src/lib/session-display.test.ts` covering an astral character at the tail boundary.
- Focused tests pass: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/lib/session-display.test.ts`.
- Lint clean: `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs ui/src/lib/session-display.ts ui/src/lib/session-display.test.ts`.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Before the patch, a peer id like `"12345😀67890"` would have produced a tail containing an isolated surrogate half. After the patch it returns `"…67890"`.
- **Real environment tested:** Local checkout of `fix/session-display-peer-id-utf16` at `8996aa6b8a`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { resolveSessionDisplayName } from "./ui/src/lib/session-display.ts"; const samples = ["agent:main:telegram:direct:491234567890", "agent:main:telegram:direct:12345😀67890"]; for (const k of samples) { const n = resolveSessionDisplayName(k); try { encodeURIComponent(n); console.log("ok"); } catch(e){ console.log("FAIL", e); } console.log(JSON.stringify(n)); }'
  ```
  And to verify the display names survive a real disk write/read round-trip:
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { resolveSessionDisplayName } from "./ui/src/lib/session-display.ts"; import { writeFileSync, readFileSync, mkdtempSync } from "node:fs"; import { tmpdir } from "node:os"; import { join } from "node:path"; const f = join(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "sd-")), "names.txt"); const samples = ["agent:main:telegram:direct:491234567890", "agent:main:telegram:direct:12345😀67890"]; const names = samples.map(resolveSessionDisplayName); writeFileSync(f, names.join("\n"), "utf8"); const r = readFileSync(f, "utf8"); console.log(r); console.log("round-trip ok:", r === names.join("\n"));'
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```
  ok
  "Telegram · …567890"
  ok
  "Telegram · …67890"

  Telegram · …567890
  Telegram · …67890
  round-trip ok: true
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** The regression test `does not split UTF-16 surrogate pairs when shortening peer ids` passes, `encodeURIComponent` succeeds on every display name, and the names survive a disk write/read round-trip.
- **What was not tested:** No live Control UI sidebar render; change is a pure string-formatting helper.

target.title: feat: trace Claude Code CLI model calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Claude Code CLI turns did not emit trusted `model.call.started`, `model.call.completed`, and `model.call.error` diagnostics. Phoenix therefore could not show a useful model span with the OpenClaw-visible prompt, response, timing, and usage data for `claude-cli` runs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add synthetic turn-level model-call tracing at the honest Claude Code CLI boundary for one-shot, managed persistent stdio, and paired-node execution. Each admitted attempt now receives exactly one terminal lifecycle event, including retry attempts, aborts, timeouts, process/parse failures, deferred background completion, persistence failure, and cleanup failure.

Content capture reuses the existing trusted capture policy and remains disabled by default. Granular capture includes only the effective OpenClaw prompt, OpenClaw-appended system prompt, and visible assistant blocks. It intentionally excludes Claude Code private prompts, hidden resume/compaction payloads, native tool schemas and arguments, raw Anthropic HTTP traffic, internal retries, upstream request IDs, and network TTFB.

Terminal cumulative usage, including cache read/write tokens, is used for the model span while existing last-assistant-message reply accounting remains unchanged.

## User Impact

Operators using OpenTelemetry/Phoenix can inspect a truthful Claude CLI model span with useful lifecycle, prompt/response, byte, timing, and aggregate usage data when content capture is explicitly enabled. Default installations remain metadata-only, and native OpenClaw/Codex tracing behavior is unchanged.

AI-assisted: yes (Codex). I reviewed the implementation and validation results.

target.title: refactor: separate external conversations from local sessions
target.body:
Closes #108666

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where agents could confuse a local model session with the external conversation attached to it. This was especially visible with Reef: a message intended for another agent could loop into the sender's local session, and waiting for a remote reply required brittle channel-target reasoning.

## Why This Change Was Made

This separates stable external `conversationRef` addresses from local session context. It adds owner-only conversation discovery, durable fire-and-forget sends, and reply-correlated turns owned by the Gateway; transports remain channel plugins, while generic delivery, queue recovery, idempotency, and reply capture live in core.

The refactor also makes Reef use one process-wide live runtime, reserves its message ID before durable queueing, and consumes an exact correlated reply inline without starting a second local agent turn. Unsolicited messages and replies that arrive after process restart continue through ordinary inbound dispatch.

The agent-scoped lease and conversation-delivery additions are combined in the unshipped v11 schema. Released pre-v11 databases migrate once into that canonical shape; no v12 schema is introduced.

## User Impact

Agents can now use `conversations_list`, `conversations_send`, and `conversations_turn` instead of treating session keys as remote destinations. Reef conversations behave like real external conversations: sends survive Gateway recovery, exact replies return to the calling tool, unrelated inbound messages still start normal turns, and multi-agent operation IDs cannot collide in the shared queue.

## Evidence

- Final head `9bdf712aba25bacefc7c81f70e4b8372f15836d4`: 80/80 outbound dispatch regressions passed, followed by the four-file `pnpm check:changed` gate.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxqbtx5ss0nekyjf46sdxdfb` ([run 29559842209](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29559842209)): rebased integration proof passed 319 assertions across 8 focused files and the full `pnpm check:changed` gate in 24m00s.
- Earlier broad proof passed all 35 changed test files across 11 Vitest shards plus `pnpm check:test-types`, `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check`, `pnpm protocol:check`, `pnpm android:i18n:check`, and `pnpm build`.
- Final conflict-free rebase regenerated and rechecked Kysely types, the SQLite sessions/transcripts schema baseline, and the Plugin SDK API baseline.
- Fresh whole-branch autoreview found one plugin-dispatch queue-persistence bypass; the accepted fix is included in the final head, regression-covered, and passed focused follow-up review with no remaining accepted/actionable findings.
- Exact-head GitHub CI is monitored through the repo-native prepare and merge gates.

target.title: fix(skill-workshop): validate apply body and show change summary before destructive writes
target.body:
Closes #107707
## Summary

Skill Workshop `applySkillProposal` could overwrite an existing SKILL.md with plan-only proposal content without validation or recovery. This fix adds canonical body validation before destructive writes, gates zero-overlap updates behind explicit approval (even under `auto` policy), and shows a bounded change summary in approval descriptions and apply results.

- Problem: `applySkillProposal` wrote stripped proposal content directly to SKILL.md with no body validation; plan/change-description proposals silently overwrote real skill content, and the default `approvalPolicy` change to `auto` (PR #107690) made this happen without user confirmation.
- Solution: Validate proposed content through the canonical `parseFrontmatter` parser (not heading heuristics), reject empty bodies, gate zero-overlap updates behind `requiresExplicitApproval` which forces pending approval even under `auto` policy, add `computeSkillChangeSummary` for `+N/-M lines` summaries, and document `rollback.json` restore path in troubleshooting.
- What changed: `src/skills/workshop/service.ts` (canonical validation + approval flag + summary), `src/skills/workshop/policy.ts` (zero-overlap forces pending approval), `src/skills/workshop/types.ts` (`changeSummary` + `requiresExplicitApproval` fields), `src/agents/tools/skill-workshop-tool.ts` (apply result text), `src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts` (6 lifecycle proof tests), `docs/tools/skill-workshop.md` (troubleshooting entries)
- What did NOT change: Generation prompts (already fixed in PR #108339), `scanProposalBundle`, `readProposalFrontmatter`, proposal frontmatter schema, rollback write logic, any config/env surface, the `proposeCreateSkill`/`proposeUpdateSkill` entry points

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [x] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Related #107707
- Related #107690 (auto-approval policy change that amplified the risk)
- Related #108339 (generation-side prompt hardening, separate from this apply-side fix)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

PR #108339 hardened generation prompts so LLMs produce full-content proposals (issue #107708), but explicitly left apply-side validation for #107707. Without apply-side checks, any plan-only or unrelated proposal body that passes the scanner (which only checks secrets/injection, not content structure) can overwrite SKILL.md. The default `approvalPolicy` change from `pending` to `auto` (PR #107690) removed the human review gate that previously caught these cases. The initial patch used heading-presence and exact-line-overlap heuristics, but Codex review identified that heading checks block valid headingless skills (the documented SKILL.md contract only requires frontmatter + markdown body, not a body heading) and that single-line overlap is trivially bypassable, while zero-overlap hard rejection leaves no path for intentional complete rewrites.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Plan-only or unrelated proposal bodies overwriting SKILL.md during apply with no validation or recovery; heading heuristic blocking valid headingless skills; zero-overlap hard rejection blocking intentional complete rewrites.

**Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 24, branch `fix/apply-body-validation-107707`, SHA `3a45f07899`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts --run
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts --run

 RUN  v4.1.10 /home/0668001188/github/20260716-2/openclaw

 ✓ |unit| src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts (41 tests) 11195ms
     ✓ applies a zero-overlap update with requiresExplicitApproval flag  465ms
     ✓ applies a plan-only update proposal with requiresExplicitApproval (no body overlap)  532ms
     ✓ rejects an empty proposal body during apply  491ms
     ✓ applies a valid headingless skill update without requiresExplicitApproval  427ms
     ✓ applies a valid full-content update and records rollback for restoration  500ms
     ✓ applies a copied-one-line plan with requiresExplicitApproval  533ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  41 passed (41)
```

Matrix evidence (apply-path validation behavior):

```
Proposal body form                              => Result
Empty body (whitespace only)                    => Hard rejection: "Proposal body is empty"
Invalid frontmatter (plan/description only)     => Hard rejection: "does not contain valid SKILL.md frontmatter"
Zero overlap with current SKILL.md              => Apply succeeds, requiresExplicitApproval=true, forced pending approval
Valid headingless skill with shared content     => Apply succeeds, requiresExplicitApproval=false
Valid full-content update with shared lines     => Apply succeeds, changeSummary returned
Copied-one-line plan (heading matches)          => Apply succeeds, requiresExplicitApproval=false (overlap detected)
```

**Observed result after fix**:
1. Empty proposal bodies are hard-rejected before SKILL.md is touched
2. Proposals without valid frontmatter (plan documents, change descriptions) are hard-rejected
3. Zero-overlap updates (unrelated replacement or plan) apply with `requiresExplicitApproval=true` and are forced through pending approval even under `auto` policy
4. Valid headingless skill updates (paragraph-style instructions) apply normally without `requiresExplicitApproval`
5. Valid full-content updates with shared lines apply normally with `changeSummary`
6. SKILL.md is never modified when hard-rejection validation fails; rollback is recorded for all successful applies

## Root Cause

`applySkillProposal` in `src/skills/workshop/service.ts` called `stripProposalFrontmatterForSkill(content)` then immediately `writeWorkspaceSkill(...)` with no validation of the resulting body content. `scanProposalBundle` only checks for secrets/injection, and `readProposalFrontmatter` only validates frontmatter name/description/status fields. The content body — the part that becomes SKILL.md — had zero validation. Combined with the default `approvalPolicy` change from `pending` to `auto` (PR #107690), plan-only proposals could be auto-applied without human review.

## Regression Test Plan

- `src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts`: 6 new tests covering empty body, invalid frontmatter, zero-overlap approval gate, headingless skill, valid apply + rollback, and copied-one-line plan
- All 35 existing tests still pass (no regressions)
- `src/skills/workshop/policy.test.ts`: 8 existing tests pass

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- When an empty proposal body is applied, a descriptive error is thrown before SKILL.md is touched
- When a proposal without valid SKILL.md frontmatter is applied, a descriptive error is thrown before SKILL.md is touched
- When a zero-overlap update proposal is applied under `auto` policy, it is forced through pending approval instead of being silently auto-applied
- When a zero-overlap update is applied (after approval), the result includes `requiresExplicitApproval: true`
- When a valid update proposal is applied, the approval description shows `Changes: +N lines, -M lines`
- Valid headingless skill updates (paragraph-style instructions) are no longer blocked

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: 6 lifecycle proof tests pass; existing 35 tests unchanged and pass
- Edge cases checked: empty body, plan-only body (zero overlap), headingless skill, copied-one-line plan, valid update with shared content, intentional complete rewrite (zero overlap + approval)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — headingless skills that were previously blocked by the heading heuristic now work; zero-overlap updates that were previously hard-rejected now go through approval gate; valid proposals with shared content continue to work unchanged
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — this aligns with the Codex review "best possible solution": validate through the existing canonical SKILL.md parser (`parseFrontmatter`), remove the heading heuristic, and provide an explicit approval-gated replacement path for intentional zero-overlap rewrites. Central apply-boundary validation is the correct owner boundary because all apply callers go through `applySkillProposal`.
- **Refactor needed**: A follow-up PR should add `restoreSkillProposal` + `skills.proposals.restore` Gateway method + CLI command. Current PR documents the manual restore path via `rollback.json` as the minimum viable solution.
- **Alternative considered**: (1) Rejecting proposals at `scanProposalBundle` time — rejected because the scanner checks secrets/injection, not content structure. (2) Heading heuristic — rejected because the documented SKILL.md contract does not require body headings, blocking valid headingless skills. (3) Zero-overlap hard rejection — rejected because it provides no path for intentional complete rewrites and the suggested `create` workaround fails (`proposeCreateSkill` rejects when the skill already exists).

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: glm-5.1 (iCodemate)
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Issue #107707 analysis; Codex review P1 findings implementation

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest-risk area**: The `requiresExplicitApproval` zero-overlap detection uses exact-line matching via `Set<string>`, which may flag intentional rewrites of very short skills (1-2 lines) where no original lines survive.
- **Mitigation**: Zero-overlap updates are not rejected — they are gated behind explicit approval, preserving the replacement path. The operator can approve the intentional rewrite. For `auto` policy, zero-overlap forces a pending approval, which is the safe default for destructive writes with no content overlap.
- **Compatibility impact**: Backward compatible — headingless skills now work (previously blocked); zero-overlap updates go through approval gate (previously hard-rejected with no workaround); valid proposals with shared content work unchanged.

target.title: fix: gateway.cmd launcher garbles non-ASCII profile paths on non-CJK Windows locales
target.body:
Closes #108774

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Windows users whose profile path contains non-ASCII characters outside the CJK range (Turkish, Cyrillic, Greek, Western European accents, ...) can install OpenClaw but the managed Gateway never starts: the generated `gateway.cmd` launcher garbles the profile path and the launch chain dies with "The system cannot find the path specified" / `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.

#107751 fixed this failure for CJK locales by encoding the launcher in the system ANSI code page — but only on locales where ANSI == OEM, and it deliberately left windows-125x hosts on plain UTF-8 ("ANSI bytes would just be a different flavor of wrong there"). On those hosts (e.g. Turkish: ANSI 1254, OEM 857) cmd.exe still reads the UTF-8 launcher in its OEM code page and the mojibake from #108774 persists.

## Why This Change Was Made

cmd.exe parses batch files with the **console code page**, which a fresh console (Task Scheduler, Startup folder, double-click) initializes from the boot-time registry `OEMCP` — not from the ANSI page, and not from whatever a parent session last `chcp`'d to. So the launcher encoder now targets the OEM page directly instead of approximating it via ANSI:

- `resolveWindowsOemEncoding()` (new, `src/infra/windows-encoding.ts`) reads `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Nls\CodePage\OEMCP` once (cached) through a narrow `queryWindowsRegistryValue` export that reuses the existing reg.exe query logic in `src/infra/windows-install-roots.ts`.
- `encodeWindowsLauncherScript` (`src/infra/windows-launcher-encoding.ts`) encodes non-ASCII `.cmd` content to that OEM page with the same `@rem openclaw-launcher-encoding=<label>` marker and fail-closed round-trip verification introduced in #107751. The `CMD_ANSI_EQUALS_OEM_ENCODINGS` special case is deleted: on CJK locales OEMCP == ACP, so those hosts resolve the identical labels (gbk/big5/shift_jis/euc-kr/windows-874) and produce byte-identical launchers — no behavior change there.
- Newly covered OEM single-byte pages: 437, 720, 737, 775, 850, 852, 855, 857, 858, 860–863, 865, 866, 869 (iconv-lite `cp###` labels; iconv-lite 0.7.2 is already a root dependency since #107751).
- The decoder is untouched — the marker mechanism was already label-generic, so launchers written by any prior version still read back correctly (including legacy `gb18030`-marked files).

Design notes:

- **Why not `%APPDATA%`/`%ProgramFiles%` substitution (the issue's suggested fix):** the ClawSweeper review on #108774 correctly notes that would break custom npm prefixes, portable Node, and version managers. This fix keeps the installer-resolved paths and makes the encoding correct instead.
- **Round-trip verification decoder:** WHATWG `TextDecoder` where its tables match Windows (gbk/big5/shift_jis/windows-874 — it also flags best-fit hazards like shift_jis `¥` → 0x5C); iconv's own decode for euc-kr (Node ICU is KS X 1001-only and false-rejects cp949/UHC extension syllables) and for all `cp###` pages (no WHATWG decoder exists; WHATWG `ibm866` even disagrees with Windows CP866 at 0x1A/0x1C/0x7F). Safe because iconv-lite never best-fits — unmappable characters become `?` and fail the round-trip, aborting the install with the existing clear error.
- **Deliberate omissions, commented in the map:** CP864 (Arabic OEM) repurposes ASCII `0x25 "%"`, which generated cmd scripts contain, and the corruption would round-trip cleanly through iconv's own model — modern Arabic Windows uses OEM 720 (included) anyway. CP1258 (Vietnamese, the one locale whose OEMCP is a windows-125x page) is omitted because iconv-lite cannot round-trip Vietnamese combining forms; it keeps today's UTF-8 fallback instead of turning mojibake into a hard install error. Hosts with the "UTF-8 worldwide" beta (OEMCP 65001) keep plain UTF-8, which is correct there.

## User Impact

`openclaw gateway install` + `gateway start` now works for Windows accounts with Turkish/Cyrillic/Greek/Western-European/etc. non-ASCII usernames — previously the P0 release-blocker path in #108774. CJK users see byte-identical output to #107751. ASCII-only installs are untouched (encoder still short-circuits before any code-page probe).

## Evidence

**Live before/after on a real affected host** — Windows 11 Pro, Turkish locale (registry ACP 1254 / OEMCP 857), i.e. exactly the ANSI≠OEM case #107751 left open. A launcher with `buildTaskScript`-shaped content (`cd /d`, `set "OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=..."`, node invocation) pointing into a `...\ev-yiğit-öğün\` profile directory, executed under a CP857 console (what Task Scheduler provides):

Before (bytes exactly as origin/main writes them on this host — UTF-8 fallback):

```
Sistem belirtilen yolu bulamıyor.            <- cd /d failed ("The system cannot find the path specified")
Error: Cannot find module 'C:\...\ev-yi─şit-├Â─ş├╝n\probe.js'   <- UTF-8 bytes misread as CP857
exit code: 1
```

After (bytes from the fixed `encodeWindowsLauncherScript()`, real production function + real registry read, which resolved `cp857` and emitted the `@rem openclaw-launcher-encoding=cp857` marker):

```
PROBE_OK cwd=C:\...\scratchpad\ev-yiğit-öğün
PROBE_OK stateDir=C:\...\scratchpad\ev-yiğit-öğün\state
exit code: 0
```

**Tests** (all pass, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ...`): `src/infra/windows-launcher-encoding.test.ts`, `src/infra/windows-encoding.test.ts`, `src/daemon/schtasks.test.ts`, `src/daemon/schtasks.install.test.ts`, `src/infra/windows-task-restart.test.ts` — 49 tests. New regression cases: cp857 Turkish path round-trip with marker, cp850 Western European, OEMCP-65001 stays UTF-8, unrepresentable characters on a single-byte OEM page fail the install fail-closed. All #107751 CJK cases (GBK/UTF-8 byte-collision, cp949 UHC syllables, 🚀 rejection) pass unchanged with OEM-based resolution.

`oxfmt` and `oxlint` clean on all touched files; `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` reports no errors in touched files (the 42 pre-existing errors on this machine reproduce identically on a clean `origin/main` checkout — local env, unrelated).

target.title: fix(music): stop hanging when generated asset downloads drip forever
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where music generation providers (e.g. fal) could hang forever when a CDN dripped the audio body slowly enough to reset per-chunk idle timers. `fetchWithTimeout` clears its abort after headers land, so the download budget no longer applied to the body.

Additionally:
1. Restores transient HTTP retry that was lost when the non-2xx validation was placed outside `executeProviderOperationWithRetry`.
2. Skips diagnostic body reads for retryable 5xx statuses so a dripping error body does not consume the shared wall-clock deadline before the retry attempt starts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three changes in `downloadGeneratedMusicAsset`:

1. **Wall-clock deadline**: One deadline spans headers + non-2xx error-detail + successful-body reads via `readResponseTextPrefix` → `readResponseWithLimit({ timeoutMs, onTimeout })`.

2. **Retry inside the wrapper**: Bounded non-2xx status validation now runs inside `executeProviderOperationWithRetry`'s operation callback. When the CDN returns HTTP 503, the error is thrown inside the retry loop so `isTransientProviderOperationError` can retry it.

3. **Skip body reads for 5xx**: Retryable statuses (500/502/503/504) cancel the response body immediately instead of reading it for diagnostics. A dripping 5xx body could otherwise consume the full wall-clock deadline, leaving the retry attempt with effectively no remaining budget.

Non-overlapping: #108982 bounds video-generation downloads; #109076 bounds Discord webhook bodies.

## User Impact

- Generated music downloads fail within the configured timeout when a CDN body trickles forever.
- Transient CDN errors (503, etc.) with dripping bodies are retried immediately — the body is cancelled so the retry gets a full budget.
- Non-retryable errors (400, etc.) still include bounded diagnostic detail.
- Music generation no longer sticks forever on a slow-drip CDN response.

## Evidence

Exact head: `dee8f741c1da3899930e3602cf858d0e6072632d`

`oxfmt --check src/music-generation/provider-assets.ts src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts` — passed.
`git diff --check` — clean.

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 ✓ bounds a dripping download body with one wall-clock deadline 284ms
 ✓ throws on non-2xx HTTP status without retry 18ms
 ✓ retries on transient HTTP status before succeeding 268ms
 ✓ skips diagnostic body read on retryable status so deadline survives for retry 264ms
 ✓ does not bound a dripping body when only chunk idle timeout is used 410ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

- **Drip body (200)**: continuous drip with timeoutMs=250 → rejects with wall-clock timeout.
- **Non-2xx (400)**: immediate 400 → throws HTTP status error without retry (400 is explicitly non-retryable), includes diagnostic body detail.
- **Retry (immediate 503 → 200)**: first request returns 503 with immediate body → retried → second request succeeds. Proves `requestCount === 2`.
- **Retry (dripping 503 → 200)**: first request returns 503 with continuous 15ms drip → body cancelled immediately (not read) → retry completes within 264ms. Proves the deadline survives for the retry attempt when the error body is skipped.
- **Negative control**: idle-only chunkTimeoutMs on a drip → stays unsettled past 400ms. Proves old code path has no wall-clock bound.

### Mutation check

Without fix (stash provider-assets.ts): `retries on transient` FAIL — 503 not retried.
With fix restored: `retries on transient` PASS — `requestCount === 2`.

### Not tested

Live fal CDN against real provider endpoints — requires real API credentials.

target.title: fix(infra): fix env-log check ordering after nonblank validation, preserve Set
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`logAcceptedEnvOption` records environment keys in a `Set` to log each accepted key once per process lifetime. The previous code ran the dedup check **before** validating that the environment value is nonblank — if a caller probed with a blank value first and a valid value later, the second call was silently suppressed.

This PR fixes the ordering issue without changing the once-only contract.

## Changes

2 files, +14/−3:

**`src/infra/env.ts`** (+2/−2)
- Move dedup check (`has()` + `add()`) after nonblank value validation, so a blank-value probe does not suppress a subsequent valid-value log for the same key
- Keep `Set<string>()` — preserves process-lifetime once-only logging, no eviction

**`src/infra/env.test.ts`** (+12/±0)
- New regression test: blank probe followed by valid value — confirms the second call produces a log entry

## Evidence

**Unit tests (11/11 passed):**
```
 ✓ logAcceptedEnvOption > records key only after accepting a nonblank value
   (blank probe does not suppress later log)
 — all 11 tests passed
```

**Lint clean**

**Real OpenClaw process proof — terminal transcript:**

Reviewed SHA: `67c0e2f0fe604921c8262a696263cce46d435767`

```
$ OPENCLAW_LOG_LEVEL=info node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/pr-proof.test.ts

Call 1 (blank): captured=0 (expect 0)

[env] OPENCLAW_PROOF_1784270570084=raw-openclaw-secret (valid call after blank)

Call 2 (valid): captured=1
  [env] OPENCLAW_PROOF_1784270570084=raw-openclaw-secret (valid call after blank)

 ✓  blank-then-valid with real logger 370ms
```

The terminal output proves:
1. **Call 1 (blank `""`)** → `captured=0`: no `[env]` line produced. The real `createSubsystemLogger` received nothing because the blank check rejected before `has()`/`add()`.
2. **Call 2 (valid `"raw-openclaw-secret"`)** → `captured=1`: exactly one real logger line emitted via the OpenClaw logging subsystem.
3. The value appears in plaintext with the `[env]` subsystem prefix — no spurious redaction, no duplicate suppression, no eviction.

## Design decision

`loggedEnv` stays as `new Set<string>()` — a bounded evicting cache (`createDedupeCache`) was originally proposed but would change the once-per-process logging contract. Since all current callers use fixed environment keys (`OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM`, `OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM_PATH`), a `Set` suffices and preserves exact deduplication.

## Review
- Manually reviewed and verified
- AI-assisted: Yes

target.title: feat(codex): surface native questions and goals
target.body:
Related: #102261
Related: #102260

## What Problem This Solves

Codex app-server runs could request structured user input or expose a native thread goal, but OpenClaw only surfaced a flattened text prompt and had no native goal command path. Control UI users could not answer the structured request in place, and operators could not read or update the upstream goal without a second state system.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the first, bounded slice of the approved Codex-parity split. It carries native `request_user_input` questions through the existing typed presentation seam into channels and the Control UI, then routes request-scoped answers back to the waiting app-server request. Secret questions stay on the warned text path and never receive an action token.

It also maps `/codex goal` read/write commands directly to upstream `thread/goal/get`, `thread/goal/set`, and `thread/goal/clear`. There is no parallel goal store. Per-thread `features.goals` remains disabled because upstream couples the feature to automatic idle continuation; the app-server RPC gate remains available from its stable process default.

The existing `turn/plan/updated` projector and Activity/UI display already landed on `main`, so this PR does not duplicate that implementation.

Upstream contract checked directly at `openai/codex@315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304`:

- [`request_user_input` method and response path](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs#L1486-L1490), [question/answer wire shapes](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs#L1585-L1637), and [response submission](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304/codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs#L1602-L1680)
- [native goal methods](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs#L539-L552), [partial set/get/clear shapes](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs#L759-L856), and [processor behavior](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_goal_processor.rs#L117-L236)
- [`turn/plan/updated` shape](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs#L411-L435) and [event projection](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304/codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs#L1192-L1246)
- [goals feature explicitly includes automatic continuation](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304/codex-rs/features/src/lib.rs#L217-L222) and [idle hook launches continuation](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304/codex-rs/ext/goal/src/extension.rs#L154-L165)

Thanks @100yenadmin for the original UI/protocol work in #102261. Contributor credit is preserved in the commit history and squash metadata.

## User Impact

Control UI users see native Codex questions as structured option/free-form cards and can submit an answer without leaving chat. Supported channels receive typed choice actions. Codex operators can inspect, set, pause, resume, block, complete, or clear the native upstream thread goal through `/codex goal`.

Automatic goal-driven follow-on turns are deliberately out of scope. Provider-neutral question RPC and autonomous continuation design remain later slices.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(infra): gateway pid probe no longer hangs when ps sampling stalls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readGatewayProcessArgsSync` (in `src/infra/gateway-processes.ts`) probes `ps` on darwin to read a gateway process's argv **before** signaling it or reporting it as a verified listener PID. The darwin branch already passed a 1000ms timeout, but {BT}spawnSync{BT} defaults `killSignal` to SIGTERM, which an unresponsive or hung `ps` child can ignore. As a result a stalled `ps` probe can keep the gateway process blocked past the configured timeout, hanging gateway signal verification and listener PID discovery.

This is the same class of stall already fixed for the doctor TUI process probe in #109243, applied to the gateway's own pid-verification path.

## Evidence

- The fix adds `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` to the `spawnSync("ps", ...)` call so a stalled probe is reaped at the deadline instead of hanging, and extracts the timeout into a named `GATEWAY_PS_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS` constant.
- Local vitest run of `src/infra/gateway-processes.test.ts` is green: 8 passed (8), including the darwin path.
- The darwin test now asserts the full `spawnSync` options shape - encoding, killSignal, timeout - locking in the behavior (mirrors the assertion added in #109243).

```ts
const ps = spawnSync("ps", ["-o", "command=", "-p", String(pid)], {
  encoding: "utf8",
  killSignal: "SIGKILL",
  timeout: GATEWAY_PS_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS,
});
```

target.title: fix(ai): bound openai-chatgpt-responses WebSocket with handshakeTimeout and maxPayload
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: The `connectWebSocket` function in `openai-chatgpt-responses` creates a WebSocket connection without any handshake timeout or message size limit. If the server accepts TCP but never completes the WebSocket upgrade, the connection hangs indefinitely. Oversized messages could also cause OOM.

**Solution**: Implement transport-neutral bounds using the existing lifecycle cleanup path rather than `ws`-specific constructor options:
- **Handshake timeout**: `setTimeout`-based 30s deadline that calls `socket.close()` and rejects the promise. Wrapped in try-catch so a throwing `close()` never leaves the promise unsettled. Works across Node, Bun, and browser globals.
- **Message size limit**: Byte-accurate enforcement in `decodeWebSocketData` using `TextEncoder` or raw `ArrayBuffer.byteLength` before materializing the JS string. Correctly bounds multibyte UTF-8 payloads unlike a simple `text.length` check.
- **Regression tests**: Stalled-handshake timeout, oversized message rejection (ASCII and multibyte), and throwing-close resilience.

**What changed**: Two files — source code and tests. ~120 lines net.

**What did NOT change**: No API changes, no `ws`-specific constructor options, no changes to `getWebSocketConstructor()`, `acquireWebSocket()`, or the SSE fallback path.

Fixes #109566

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Unbounded WebSocket handshake wait and oversized message OOM risk

**Real environment tested**: Node.js v24.13.1 / Linux / ws library / net module controlled server

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
npx tsx evidence-collect.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
━━ Test 1: Stalled WebSocket handshake → timeout ━━
  [server] TCP listening on 127.0.0.1:28760
  [server] TCP accepted, holding without upgrade...
  [server] received 377 bytes (WS upgrade request), ignoring
  ✅ connectWebSocket rejected after 5034ms
  ✅ Error: WebSocket connection handshake timed out
  ✅ Timeout accuracy: PASS (expected ~5000ms, got 5034ms)

━━ Test 2: Oversized message → close code 1009 ━━
  [server] WS server listening on 127.0.0.1:28761
  [server] WebSocket upgrade complete
  [client] Sending oversized message (17.0 MiB)
  ✅ Oversized message rejected with CodexProtocolError
  ✅ Error: WebSocket message exceeds maximum size of 16777216 bytes
  ✅ Close code 1009 (Message Too Big) was sent to peer

━━ Test 3: Byte accuracy — multibyte UTF-8 payload ━━
  Character: € (U+20AC) — 3 UTF-8 bytes, 1 UTF-16 code unit
  UTF-16 length (text.length, BEFORE fix): 5941932 chars  (UNDER limit)
  UTF-8  length (TextEncoder, AFTER fix):  17825796 bytes (OVER limit)
  ✅ Byte-accurate check correctly catches multibyte payloads
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All three bounds are verified with real controlled-server evidence. Handshake timeout correctly fires at ~5s with the expected error message. Oversized messages are rejected with close code 1009. Multibyte UTF-8 payloads that would pass a naive `text.length` check are correctly caught by the byte-accurate enforcement.

**What was not tested**: No real OpenAI API call. Evidence uses controlled local TCP/WS servers. SSE fallback path (unchanged) not tested.

---

## Tests and validation

4 regression tests:
1. Stalled handshake timeout — connectWebSocketForTest rejects after deadline
2. Oversized ASCII message — parseWebSocket rejects > 16 MiB payload
3. Multibyte oversized message — non-ASCII payload correctly bounded by byte count
4. Throwing-close resilience — socket.close() throwing during handshake timeout does not prevent promise settlement

## Risk checklist

- [x] Backwards compatible — no API changes
- [x] Transport-neutral — works on Node, Bun, browser globals
- [x] Byte-accurate — correct for multibyte UTF-8 payloads
- [x] Throwing-close guard — promise always settled
- [x] merge-risk: low — ~120 lines net, regression tests + real evidence

target.title: refactor: move non-session runtime journals to SQLite
target.body:
Related: #98236

AI-assisted: yes. The complete branch diff was reviewed with the repo autoreview workflow; all findings were addressed before publication.

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where several OpenClaw-owned runtime journals still wrote JSONL files even though current storage policy requires app state and caches to live in SQLite. Those file writers bypassed the shared/per-agent state ownership model and left legacy paths in steady-state runtime code.

The session/transcript store was deliberately excluded because #98236 owns that completed SQLite flip.

## Why This Change Was Made

The remaining state writers now use the narrowest existing SQLite owner: shared diagnostic events for core audit journals, Memory Core plugin state for memory-host events, and the per-agent database for ACP parent-stream diagnostics. Legacy persistent audit/event files import only through explicit `openclaw doctor --fix` migrations; audit imports require exclusive state ownership, verify SQLite rows, sanitize the retired source, and only then archive it. ACP diagnostic files are rebuildable and receive no compatibility importer. There are no runtime fallback readers or dual writes.

### Audit classification

| Surface | Observed role | Policy classification | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src/config/io.audit.ts` (`logs/config-audit.jsonl`) | Core config-write/observe audit writer | Shared state DB, `diagnostic_events` / `config-audit` | Migrated; redacted records; bounded to latest 50,000 rows; legacy import and archive owned by doctor only |
| `src/system-agent/audit.ts` (`audit/system-agent.jsonl`, retired Crestodian path) | Core system-agent mutation audit writer | Shared state DB, `diagnostic_events` / `system-agent-audit` | Migrated; bounded to latest 50,000 rows; legacy import and archive owned by doctor only |
| `src/memory-host-sdk/events.ts` (`memory/.dreams/events.jsonl`) | Memory recall/promotion/dream event state consumed by status, public artifacts, and Memory Wiki | Memory Core plugin KV in shared SQLite | Migrated with per-workspace append ordering; doctor imports legacy source lines ahead of SQLite-native events; public artifact is now a virtual JSON artifact backed by SQLite |
| `src/agents/acp-spawn-parent-stream.ts` (`*.acp-stream.jsonl`) | Child-session ACP parent-stream diagnostic state | Per-agent DB, `acp_parent_stream_events` | Migrated; rows are session-owned and cascade on session deletion; writes batch synchronously, retry with backoff, and cap pending diagnostics; old transient files are not imported |
| `src/infra/session-cost-usage.ts` | Reads legacy/archive transcript JSONL; rollups already use per-agent SQLite | Excluded session/transcript area; no JSONL writer | Left unchanged; #98236 owns session/transcript storage |
| `src/security/fix.ts` | Repairs permissions on excluded transcript artifacts | Excluded session/transcript maintenance; no writer | Left unchanged |
| `src/infra/backup-volatile-filter.ts` | Names/filter rules inside backup production | Named backup artifact | Left unchanged |
| `src/agents/cache-trace.ts`, `src/agents/anthropic-payload-log.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.raw-stream.ts`, `src/logging/diagnostic-*`, channel delivery trace | Explicit opt-in traces, raw provider capture, or support bundles | Named diagnostic/log artifacts | Left unchanged |
| CLI runner/Claude session files, transcript/session-manager paths, hooks, compaction checkpoints, session inspection/branching | Provider/external-tool contracts or the excluded session/transcript surface | External tool contract or #98236-owned session artifact | Left unchanged |
| `src/trajectory/{runtime-file,paths,cleanup,types}.ts` | SQLite runtime plus explicit trajectory export/legacy discovery | Named export artifact; no steady-state JSONL app-state writer | Left unchanged |

The post-change discovery still finds legacy migration constants and legitimate artifact/wire/session references, but no additional non-session OpenClaw-owned runtime JSONL writer.

target.title: fix(gateway): reap stale MCP processes on session reset regardless of…
target.body:
Closes #92569

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where resetting or deleting a session could leave its MCP child processes running when the embedded agent run did not stop within the 15-second grace period. Those stale processes could keep file locks or ports that the replacement session needs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gateway cleanup now requests MCP retirement before waiting for the embedded run, but uses the existing lease-aware retirement contract instead of immediately closing transports. A runtime with active tool, app-view, or request leases remains alive; normal agent-run materialization now completes deferred retirement as soon as the final lease releases.

This replaces the original immediate-disposal patch, which could close MCP transports under in-flight work.

## User Impact

Session reset and delete no longer skip MCP cleanup on the timeout path. In-flight MCP work is preserved until it releases its lease, after which the old runtime and child processes are removed without waiting for the idle TTL.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** an active MCP runtime must be marked for cleanup during reset/delete without killing its child process while an in-flight run still owns a lease.
- **Real environment tested:** secretless GitHub Actions runner, Ubuntu 24.04, Node 24, PR head `666ebeb9978` plus a temporary proof-only workflow commit. The proof branch was deleted after the run.
- **Exact steps or command run:** `node --import tsx --input-type=module` started a real stdio MCP child through the production session runtime, materialized its tools to acquire a run lease, requested `retireSessionMcpRuntime({ preserveActiveLeases: true })`, then released the materialized runtime.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture from the successful `node` process-lifecycle run: https://github.com/zhanxingxin1998/openclaw/actions/runs/29503144525

```json
{
  "activeLeasesAfterRetirementRequest": 1,
  "childAliveWhileLeaseHeld": true,
  "sessionCachedWhileLeaseHeld": true,
  "childExitedAfterFinalLeaseRelease": true,
  "sessionRemovedAfterFinalLeaseRelease": true
}
```

- **Observed result after fix:** the retirement request does not interrupt active MCP work; releasing the final run lease immediately completes deferred retirement, removes the session runtime, and terminates the real MCP child process.
- **What was not tested:** a full live Gateway RPC with an intentionally hung model provider and a real SQLite/LadybugDB lock. The real MCP process/lease lifecycle is covered directly, while reset and delete timeout routing is covered by Gateway integration tests.

### Regression coverage

- `src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts`: production manager/materialization coverage, including a real stdio MCP child process (`75/75` locally).

target.title: fix(browser): keep tab reachability retry delay abortable
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where cancelling a browser tab operation during the reachability retry delay would wait the full delay before responding to the cancellation.

`ensureBrowserRunning` used `new Promise(setTimeout)` for the 250ms retry delay between reachability probes. When the request `AbortSignal` fired during this delay, the function waited the entire `TAB_REACHABILITY_RETRY_DELAY_MS` before calling `signal.throwIfAborted()`, adding unnecessary latency to cancellation-sensitive callers.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retry delay now uses `sleepWithAbort(TAB_REACHABILITY_RETRY_DELAY_MS, signal)` which rejects immediately when the signal fires, so the caller is notified of the cancellation during the delay rather than after it.

Related prior art: #108561 (discord gateway READY retry abortSignal), #108408 (feishu retry abortSignal propagation).

## User Impact

Browser tab operations (close, focus, select) cancelled during the 250ms reachability retry window respond to user cancellation up to 250ms faster.

## Evidence

### Scope

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Head | `eac9fd9a2f5` |
| Files | `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.ts` (+4/−5) · `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.test.ts` (+1/−1) |
| Net | +5 / −6 across 2 files |

### Production change (behavior)

```ts
// Before
await new Promise((resolve) => { setTimeout(resolve, RETRY_DELAY_MS); });
signal?.throwIfAborted();

// After
await sleepWithAbort(TAB_REACHABILITY_RETRY_DELAY_MS, signal);
```

### Real-timer timing proof

A standalone Node.js script (`scripts/proof-109536-abort-timing.mjs`) compares the two patterns with real `performance.now()` timers and a real `AbortController`. Each scenario is run 5 times with the abort signal firing 50ms into the 250ms retry delay:

```
--- BEFORE (old code) ---
  Run 1: 250.6 ms  ✗ ABORTED (This operation was aborted)
  Run 2: 250.8 ms  ✗ ABORTED (This operation was aborted)
  Run 3: 250.3 ms  ✗ ABORTED (This operation was aborted)
  Run 4: 251.0 ms  ✗ ABORTED (This operation was aborted)
  Run 5: 250.2 ms  ✗ ABORTED (This operation was aborted)

--- AFTER (new code: sleepWithAbort) ---
  Run 1: 50.5 ms  ✗ ABORTED (aborted)
  Run 2: 50.6 ms  ✗ ABORTED (aborted)
  Run 3: 50.5 ms  ✗ ABORTED (aborted)
  Run 4: 51.0 ms  ✗ ABORTED (aborted)
  Run 5: 50.8 ms  ✗ ABORTED (aborted)
```

- **BEFORE**: consistently ~250ms — always waits the full retry delay before noticing the abort.
- **AFTER**: consistently ~50ms — rejects as soon as the abort signal fires, eliminating up to 200ms of unnecessary wait.

The same abort-propagation invariant is additionally covered by the fake-timer unit test at `tabs.test.ts:345`.

### Local gates (touched surface)

| Gate | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit | `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.test.ts` | **22 passed** / 1 file |

### Proof

The existing test "does not retry or mutate after cancellation during the retry delay" covers this scenario: it advances past the first reachability check, aborts the signal, then verifies no reachability retry occurred. With `sleepWithAbort`, the abort is detected immediately during the delay rather than after it expires, and the error message changes from `"cancelled"` (from `throwIfAborted`) to `"aborted"` (from `sleepWithAbort`).

Real-timer proof confirms the timing improvement holds with real wall-clock timers, not only with fake timers.

---

target.title: fix(ai): bound openai-chatgpt-responses WebSocket with handshakeTimeout and maxPayload
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: The `connectWebSocket` function in `openai-chatgpt-responses` creates a WebSocket connection without any handshake timeout or message size limit. If the server accepts TCP but never completes the WebSocket upgrade, the connection hangs indefinitely. Oversized messages could also cause OOM.

**Solution**: Implement transport-neutral bounds using the existing lifecycle cleanup path rather than `ws`-specific constructor options:
- **Handshake timeout**: `setTimeout`-based 30s deadline that calls `socket.close()` and rejects the promise. Wrapped in try-catch so a throwing `close()` never leaves the promise unsettled. Works across Node, Bun, and browser globals.
- **Message size limit**: Byte-accurate enforcement in `decodeWebSocketData` using `TextEncoder` or raw `ArrayBuffer.byteLength` before materializing the JS string. Correctly bounds multibyte UTF-8 payloads unlike a simple `text.length` check.
- **Regression tests**: Stalled-handshake timeout, oversized message rejection (ASCII and multibyte), and throwing-close resilience.

**What changed**: Two files — source code and tests. ~120 lines net.

**What did NOT change**: No API changes, no `ws`-specific constructor options, no changes to `getWebSocketConstructor()`, `acquireWebSocket()`, or the SSE fallback path.

Fixes #109566

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Unbounded WebSocket handshake wait and oversized message OOM risk

**Real environment tested**: Node.js v24.13.1 / Linux / ws library / net module controlled server

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
npx tsx evidence-collect.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
━━ Test 1: Stalled WebSocket handshake → timeout ━━
  [server] TCP listening on 127.0.0.1:28760
  [server] TCP accepted, holding without upgrade...
  [server] received 377 bytes (WS upgrade request), ignoring
  ✅ connectWebSocket rejected after 5034ms
  ✅ Error: WebSocket connection handshake timed out
  ✅ Timeout accuracy: PASS (expected ~5000ms, got 5034ms)

━━ Test 2: Oversized message → close code 1009 ━━
  [server] WS server listening on 127.0.0.1:28761
  [server] WebSocket upgrade complete
  [client] Sending oversized message (17.0 MiB)
  ✅ Oversized message rejected with CodexProtocolError
  ✅ Error: WebSocket message exceeds maximum size of 16777216 bytes
  ✅ Close code 1009 (Message Too Big) was sent to peer

━━ Test 3: Byte accuracy — multibyte UTF-8 payload ━━
  Character: € (U+20AC) — 3 UTF-8 bytes, 1 UTF-16 code unit
  UTF-16 length (text.length, BEFORE fix): 5941932 chars  (UNDER limit)
  UTF-8  length (TextEncoder, AFTER fix):  17825796 bytes (OVER limit)
  ✅ Byte-accurate check correctly catches multibyte payloads
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All three bounds are verified with real controlled-server evidence. Handshake timeout correctly fires at ~5s with the expected error message. Oversized messages are rejected with close code 1009. Multibyte UTF-8 payloads that would pass a naive `text.length` check are correctly caught by the byte-accurate enforcement.

**What was not tested**: No real OpenAI API call. Evidence uses controlled local TCP/WS servers. SSE fallback path (unchanged) not tested.

---

## Tests and validation

4 regression tests:
1. Stalled handshake timeout — connectWebSocketForTest rejects after deadline
2. Oversized ASCII message — parseWebSocket rejects > 16 MiB payload
3. Multibyte oversized message — non-ASCII payload correctly bounded by byte count
4. Throwing-close resilience — socket.close() throwing during handshake timeout does not prevent promise settlement

## Risk checklist

- [x] Backwards compatible — no API changes
- [x] Transport-neutral — works on Node, Bun, browser globals
- [x] Byte-accurate — correct for multibyte UTF-8 payloads
- [x] Throwing-close guard — promise always settled
- [x] merge-risk: low — ~120 lines net, regression tests + real evidence

target.title: fix(agents): preserve thinking default precedence for listed agents
target.body:
<!-- submission-timestamps:start -->
First submitted: July 17, 2026, 12:05 AM (US Eastern Time) / 04:05 UTC.
Last body edit: July 17, 2026, 2:09 AM (US Eastern Time) / 06:09 UTC.
Latest head commit: July 17, 2026, 1:37 AM (US Eastern Time) / 05:37 UTC.
<!-- submission-timestamps:end -->

Closes #109276

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an inconsistency where `resolveAgentConfig()` returned only an explicit
`agents.list[].thinkingDefault` value even though its contract says that agent
defaults have already been applied. Callers that inspect the resolved config
could therefore observe `undefined` for a listed agent while the effective
runtime later inherited `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` through another
resolution path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The direct nullish fallback suggested by the issue is incomplete on its own.
Several runtime callers intentionally treat the value from the agent entry as
an explicit override before evaluating per-model `params.thinking`, the global
default, and provider/model defaults. Returning the merged global value through
those override-sensitive paths would make the global default incorrectly win
over a per-model setting.

This change separates the two contracts:

- `resolveAgentConfig()` now returns the documented merged value.
- `resolveAgentThinkingDefaultOverride()` returns only the explicit per-agent
  value for precedence-sensitive runtime paths.

The command, reply model-selection, subagent inheritance, gateway session, and
startup-summary paths use the explicit helper where provenance matters.

## User Impact

Consumers of `resolveAgentConfig()` can now rely on a listed agent inheriting
`agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`. Existing runtime precedence remains intact:

1. session or message override
2. explicit per-agent default
3. per-model `params.thinking`
4. global `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`
5. provider/model default

Explicit `off` values remain authoritative because the merge uses nullish, not
truthy, fallback semantics.

## Breaking Changes

None expected. This restores the documented merged-config contract while
preserving the existing runtime precedence order.

## Implementation

- Add `resolveAgentThinkingDefaultOverride()` at the agent-scope owner boundary.
- Merge `thinkingDefault` in `resolveAgentConfig()` with agent-over-global
  nullish precedence.
- Route precedence-sensitive callers through the explicit override helper.
- Add focused tests for merged inheritance, explicit `off`, and a listed agent
  whose per-model thinking setting must still outrank the global default.

## Code-Path Analysis

- Owner: `src/agents/agent-scope-config.ts`
- Public facade: `src/agents/agent-scope.ts`
- Runtime callers: `src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.ts`,
  `src/agents/command/model-selection.ts`, `src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts`,
  `src/gateway/session-utils.ts`, `src/gateway/server-startup-log.ts`
- Adjacent precedence owner: `src/agents/model-thinking-default.ts`
- Tests: `src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts`,
  `src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.test.ts`, plus existing command,
  subagent, gateway-session, and startup-summary coverage
- Contract: `src/config/types.agents.ts` and `docs/tools/thinking.md`

## Mainline Comparison

- Official base: `OpenClaw/OpenClaw:main@399345e1bb1b472969cf586bd1400536e940a3cc`
- Base fetched/verified: July 17, 2026, 05:37 UTC
- Current main still returned only `entry.thinkingDefault` from the merged
  resolver. Recent same-surface changes did not implement this provenance split.

## Branch/Base Provenance

- Base: `OpenClaw/OpenClaw:main@399345e1bb1b472969cf586bd1400536e940a3cc`
- Head: `snowzlmbot/OpenClaw:fix/109276-thinking-default-fallback@c58a6f981f64167e33806c0bf936121d13db704b`
- The head branch was created/replayed directly from the official base.
- The fork default branch was not used as the implementation baseline and was
  not modified by this work.

## Dependency/Contract Verification

No external dependency contract changed. The configuration type already states
that `agents.list[].thinkingDefault` overrides
`agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`, and the thinking documentation already
defines per-model thinking ahead of the global default. The implementation now
preserves both contracts explicitly.

## Labels Considered

- `agents`
- `P2`
- `impact:auth-provider`
- `merge-risk: compatibility` because configuration-default precedence is
  compatibility-sensitive

These are suggestions only; this contribution does not claim maintainer label
authority.

## Validation

## Summary

- Emit Codex `final_answer` candidates as ephemeral Activity events with candidate, superseded, and selected lifecycle states.
- Select only the authoritative candidate at successful turn completion; late tool work invalidates an earlier candidate until a replacement arrives.
- Render candidate lifecycle in the current Control UI Activity page without transcript persistence or channel progress.

## Why

Codex may emit a final-answer candidate, reopen the same turn for injected work or a tool, then emit a second authoritative candidate. Activity should expose that lifecycle for operators without leaking provisional text into chat or messaging channels.

The implementation follows the upstream Codex contract: `MessagePhase::FinalAnswer` is the terminal answer for the current turn, while explicit same-turn work can reopen the turn. The regression fixture covers candidate one, late tool work, candidate two, and authoritative `turn/completed` selection. target.title: fix(agents): keep bundle LSP tool names provider-safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users enabling bundled LSP servers with human-readable server keys could expose invalid or colliding agent tool names when those keys contain spaces, punctuation, numeric prefixes, or overlap with an existing registered tool name.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bundle LSP runtime now keeps the original server key for user-facing labels and execution details while deriving provider-safe model-facing names for hover, definition, and references tools. Complete tool names that are already valid, such as `lsp_hover_123`, are preserved for compatibility; unsafe, overlong, or colliding complete names are still bounded and disambiguated within the existing 64-character tool-name budget.

## User Impact

Agents can use bundled LSP hover, definition, and references tools for readable server names such as `Type Script!` or numeric keys. Existing policy that matches valid numeric-key tool names such as `lsp_definition_123` continues to match after upgrade, while unsafe or colliding names are repaired before registration.

## Evidence

- Current refreshed head: `e2600bc973e99d029f12c6a1abb7e6b3c38bda8e`.
- Exact-head GitHub proof at `e2600bc973e99d029f12c6a1abb7e6b3c38bda8e`: `Real behavior proof`, `check-lint`, `check-test-types`, `check-prod-types`, `build-artifacts`, and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed.
- Current-head repair: bundled LSP tool materialization preserves already-valid complete numeric-key names such as `lsp_hover_123`, `lsp_definition_123`, and `lsp_references_123`.

target.title: fix(cli): guard plugins JSON.parse against malformed input
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readJsonFile()` in `plugins-authoring-command.ts` calls `JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(...))` without try-catch. If `package.json` or `openclaw.plugin.json` is malformed, the user gets a raw `SyntaxError` with no file path context, making it hard to diagnose which file is broken.

## Why This Change Was Made

This follows the same JSON.parse guard pattern that has been merged in 12+ community PRs (lsr911, solodmd, Pick-cat, etc.) — wrapping JSON.parse in try-catch with a descriptive error message that includes the file path.

## Evidence

**Before fix**: malformed `package.json` produces raw `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ...` with no file context.

**After fix**: `Error: Malformed JSON in /path/to/package.json` with the original error preserved as `cause`.

**Test**: Added test "throws a user-friendly error when package.json is malformed JSON" — writes `{invalid json` to `package.json`, runs build command, verifies error message contains "Malformed JSON in".

```
✓ throws a user-friendly error when package.json is malformed JSON
```

## Merge Risk

Low. The change only wraps JSON.parse in try-catch; the error message uses the existing `formatOutputPath()` helper for consistent path formatting. Original error is preserved as `cause` for debugging.

target.title: fix(plugin-sdk): guard assertHttpUrlTargetsPrivateNetwork against malformed URLs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where callers of the public plugin-sdk SSRF helper `assertHttpUrlTargetsPrivateNetwork` would receive an uncaught `TypeError: Invalid URL` when given malformed input, instead of a controlled application error.

## Why This Change Was Made

The helper now wraps `new URL(url)` in try/catch and throws `Error("Invalid URL: …")`, matching the defensive pattern already used by sibling helpers in the same file (for example `isHttpsUrlAllowedByHostnameSuffixAllowlist`). Valid HTTP/HTTPS policy checks are unchanged.

## User Impact

Plugin and channel code that validates self-hosted HTTP endpoints now gets a predictable typed error for malformed URLs, making setup failures easier to diagnose without leaking raw URL constructor exceptions.

## Evidence

**Before (upstream/main):**
```
error name: TypeError
error message: Invalid URL
```

**Premise (sibling pattern in the same file):**
`isHttpsUrlAllowedByHostnameSuffixAllowlist` already wraps `new URL(url)` in try/catch.

**After (this branch):**
```
error name: Error
error message: Invalid URL: not-a-url
```

Harness (real exported function, no mocks):
```bash
node --import tsx -e "
import { assertHttpUrlTargetsPrivateNetwork } from './src/plugin-sdk/ssrf-policy.ts';
try {
  await assertHttpUrlTargetsPrivateNetwork('not-a-url', { dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork: true });
} catch (err) {
  console.log('error name:', err?.constructor?.name);
  console.log('error message:', err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err));
}
"
```

target.title: fix(whatsapp): add chunk-idle timeout to inbound media download
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where WhatsApp inbound media downloads that stall after Baileys returns a stream (headers/start ok, then no further chunks) would block `downloadInboundMedia` forever via `saveMediaStream`'s unbounded `for await`, so inbound dispatch never produces an agent reply for that message.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Wrap the Baileys AsyncIterable with a local per-chunk idle race (production default `30_000` ms), matching Telegram's download idle floor and the Feishu channel pattern.
- On timeout, explicitly **destroy** the source (if it supports `destroy`) so the underlying Readable/HTTP resource closes, then call `iterator.return()` without awaiting. Silence the losing `nextPromise` to avoid unhandledRejection.
- **Do NOT `await` iterator.return()** in the finally block — Node Readable async-iterator `return()` hangs when the underlying source is stalled.
- Extract `saveInboundMediaStreamWithIdleTimeout` as the production save chokepoint so loopback proofs drive the exact path Baileys streams enter.
- ClawSweeper Maintainer option 1 asked for live WhatsApp timeout+recovery. This refresh supplies the strongest **local-server** proof at the Baileys Readable/HTTP boundary (timeout + destroy + server connection close + healthy progressing path), without live credentials. Live multi-message dispatch remains explicitly out of scope below.

Collision check: searched open PRs for "whatsapp chunk-idle timeout media download stall"; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found.

## User Impact

- **Before**: A stalled Baileys media stream would hang inbound dispatch indefinitely — no agent reply, no error logged.
- **After**: Stream times out after 30s idle with `WhatsAppInboundMediaTimeoutError`. The source is destroyed so the HTTP resource closes. Normal progressing streams are unaffected.

## Verification

- Exact head: `824c346b4a86a37224424e203aae2031e6a04c3e`
- `oxfmt` on touched WhatsApp inbound media files — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed; exit 0.
- Focused tests:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/media.node.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/media.idle.proof.test.ts -- --run
```

```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  19 passed (19)
```

- Mutation check: removing `destroySource(source)` makes HTTP loopback `destroyed=true` / `server_close=true` fail; restoring passes.
- Rebased onto latest `origin/main` before this proof refresh.

## Evidence

See **Real behavior proof** for exact `node --import tsx` transcript. Vitest includes the same HTTP `IncomingMessage` case.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: chunk-idle timeout on stalled WhatsApp/Baileys-like media download stream, with source destroy + HTTP connection close.
Real environment tested: Node 22, production `saveInboundMediaStreamWithIdleTimeout` / `saveMediaStream`, local `node:http` on `127.0.0.1` (headers flushed, body stalled), Node `IncomingMessage` Readable — same boundary Baileys stream downloads expose. No live WhatsApp session.
Exact commands run:

```bash
node --import tsx extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/proof-whatsapp-media-chunk-idle.mts
```

Observed output after fix:

```text
node=v22.22.0
head=824c346b4a86a37224424e203aae2031e6a04c3e

[case 1] negative control — stalled HTTP body without idle wrap
  ok: stalled HTTP Readable without idle wrap stays pending (>300ms)
  info: outcome=still-pending wait_ms=302 without_idle_wrap=true

[case 2] positive control — stalled HTTP body with idle wrap
  ok: timed out (not resolved)
  ok: error is WhatsAppInboundMediaTimeoutError
  ok: timeout fires within 3s
  ok: timeout fires after the idle budget
  ok: source Readable is destroyed after timeout
  ok: server observed client/connection close after destroy
  info: elapsed_ms=86 timed_out=true destroyed=true server_close=true chunkTimeoutMs=80

[case 3] valid response — progressing HTTP body
  ok: saved media size matches input
  ok: contentType preserved
  info: size=4 contentType=image/jpeg timed_out=false

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 9 passed, 0 failed
```

Evidence:
- Negative control: stalled HTTP body without idle wrap stays pending (`outcome=still-pending`)
- Positive control: idle wrap rejects with `WhatsAppInboundMediaTimeoutError`, `destroyed=true`, `server_close=true`
- Valid path: progressing HTTP JPEG saves (`size=4 timed_out=false`)
- Vitest HTTP case asserts the same destroy + server close contract

What was not tested: Live WhatsApp/Baileys cloud media download, real device session, or end-to-end subsequent-message dispatch after a live stall. Proof is controlled local-server at the Node Readable/HTTP boundary.

## Risk / Compatibility

Low. Wraps an existing AsyncIterable with a timeout raceguard. No new config/env. Progressing streams unchanged. Timeout destroys the source Readable so sockets do not accumulate after releasing the agent workflow. AI-assisted.

target.title: fix(webhooks): keep routes cold when SecretRefs are unavailable
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an unavailable webhook route SecretRef was resolved on each public request, hiding the typed failure cause from Gateway startup diagnostics and bypassing the runtime owner-isolation snapshot. Inline env-template refs also needed an unambiguous cold state without rejecting a successfully resolved literal that happens to use template syntax.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Webhooks plugin now declares route secrets through its manifest contract. Startup materializes each route independently; failed shorthand refs are canonicalized back to structured SecretRefs, so only that route stays cold while healthy siblings continue. Public failures remain generic `401 unauthorized`, while the secrets runtime records the exact route owner and typed resolution reason.

## User Impact

Operators can keep the Gateway and healthy webhook routes available when one route secret is unavailable. The cold route fails closed, public callers receive no secret-resolution detail, and startup logs identify the exact degraded route and cause. Secret rotation now takes effect through Gateway reload or restart rather than public-request-time resolution.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/webhooks/src/http.test.ts src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-plugins.bundled.test.ts src/plugins/manifest-registry.test.ts` — 118 tests passed.
